# What BabelGlobalKreole does — and does not — claim

BabelGlobalKreole is a public, evidence-grounded framework for documenting, comparing, and responsibly applying knowledge about Creole languages and related language-design work. It is designed to link to existing scholarly and community resources rather than silently replace them.

## What it aims to do

- Make language-related records more findable, comparable, and reusable.
- Keep source provenance, uncertainty, rights, and consent visible.
- Help applications and tools consume versioned, machine-readable information.
- Support education, research, localization, creative work, and other applications without letting any one application redefine the framework.

## What it does not claim

- It does not claim that all Creoles are one language.
- It does not replace language communities, speakers, or existing scholarly resources.
- It does not present proposed or fictional language material as evidence about real languages.
- It is not a complete comparative corpus, exhaustive lexicon, finished grammar, or validated universal language.
- Listing a source does not itself grant permission to reproduce its contents.

## How to use it responsibly

Check the evidence policy and the record's source locations before reusing a claim. Preserve distinctions between verified facts, source-reported claims, interpretation, hypotheses, and creative proposals. When evidence or rights are unclear, record the uncertainty rather than filling the gap with a guess.

## Next steps

Start with the [project README](https://github.com/Francois-EF-WebOps/BabelGlobalKreole#start-here), [evidence policy](https://github.com/Francois-EF-WebOps/BabelGlobalKreole/blob/main/docs/evidence-policy.md), and [contributing guide](https://github.com/Francois-EF-WebOps/BabelGlobalKreole/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Corrections and sourced resource suggestions are welcome through the repository's issue templates.

## Sources and status

This is an owner-authored summary of the project's own scope statements, not an independent linguistic assessment. The project remains a framework bootstrap and its contents have varying evidence and maturity levels. Review this page when the project scope or evidence policy changes.
